submitter: bugs_closed/283 lane (RFC_032 step 3, Half A) — the successor building thread
rationale:
THE DEFECT, still live at the served artefact as I write this. A repeatable component's element ids are namespaced with {{.InstanceID}} = InstanceToken(function, occurrence), the occurrence counting same-function predecessors on the page in position order. That rule is canonical (InstanceCounter.Next). The two render paths that see ONE section at a time — RenderComponentAction (build / content_rewrite) and the section editor — supplied a CONSTANT occurrence 0 to every instance, so any per-section render re-collided every multi-instance page it touched. Three of the twelve pages repaired on 2026-08-23 were re-collided within hours by an unrelated lane's backfill. Verified 2026-08-24 by fetching the pages: gaswholesalers.com/pricing-transparency.html and vetcomparison.uk/how-it-works.html each serve id="c-generic-text-block" TWICE.

THE FIX. Neither path invents a second rule; both feed the SAME rule its real INPUT.
  * BUILD PATH: it is always a loop iteration. Loop expansion already injects loop_item_index and loop_name into each substep's OWN config and parks every item in CollectedData. So the occurrence is counted from the sections already rendered IN THIS PASS — the same arithmetic InstanceCounter does, over the same list, one section at a time.
  * EDITOR PATH: no loop, but it holds the stored row, so it counts same-function predecessors in the database, position-exact, with a (position, id) tie arm.
  * EVERYTHING ELSE: constant 0, exactly today's behaviour.

WHY THIS SHAPE RATHER THAN THE COMMITTED PLAN'S. The committed PLAN (2026-08-24) proposed a DB lookup on BOTH paths, using slot_name + a same-slot rank on the build path, activated by a new page_id_from workflow-config key. I am superseding its Half A for three measured reasons, and the council should judge the substitution as much as the code. (1) It declared a residue it called irreducible: on a page's FIRST build no page_components rows exist, so every instance gets 0 and a new multi-instance page still collides. Counting the loop's own items closes that, because the list being counted is the list being rendered. (2) It needed slot-name matching to disambiguate the 16-of-30 multi-instance pairs that repeat a slot_name — and slot names are unreliable by this repo's own record (v3_site_actions.go:1203 on pages.sections vs page_components.slot_name; bugs_open/182 on positional slots like "prose-0"). Loop counting never consults a slot. (3) Its config key made the fix INERT until a migration landed. This ships no migration at all and is live at the image roll.

WHY READING THE LOOP KEYS IS NOT COUPLING TO ANOTHER COMPONENT'S INTERNALS — the objection I expect and the one I have tried hardest to answer with evidence rather than argument. loop_item_index and loop_name arrive on the step's own config by the same channel as every other config key; they are DECLARED platform surface in datahelpers.frameworkStepConfigKeys ("injected by loop expansion", never unknown to the config-key audit); and an action in the same package (LoopCompleteAction) has read loop_name and the item keys for months. The one genuinely fragile part was the item key's SPELLING, which existed as three separate literals — this change single-sources it as datahelpers.LoopItemKey and adds a cross-package test that drives the REAL expander and asserts the REAL reader agrees with it. That test is why the coupling claim is enforceable rather than asserted.

SAFETY. Every branch that cannot derive binds occurrence 0 and nothing here can fail a render — the derivation is an input-improver, never a gate; a lookup error yields a warning and 0. Against the constant-0 status quo the change is monotonically non-worse within the set of sections a path renders: under constant 0 every same-function pair already collides, so a derived assignment can only MERGE pairs already merged, never create a new collision. The single exception is the errs-high editor case (risk 2 below).

This change also deletes the last of RFC_032 section 8's three ComponentID bindings (v3_site_actions.go:2385), twice deferred because that file kept carrying other sessions' uncommitted hunks. It is folded in here because this change edits the same function anyway.

plan.summary: The two single-section render paths stop stamping a constant occurrence 0: the build path counts its own loop's already-rendered items, the section editor counts stored predecessors position-exactly, and constant 0 becomes the universal fallback. The loop item-key spelling is single-sourced and pinned by a cross-package parity test against the real expander. No migration, no config key: live at the roll.

edits.rationale: The "<loop_name>_item_<index>" spelling is a contract between four places that never call each other (the expander writes it; setLoopVariable and LoopCompleteAction read it; this change's occurrence reader now counts it). It existed as THREE separate literals. A typo in any one produces a MISS, not an error — and every reader treats "key absent" as a legitimate empty case — so the drift would present as a quietly wrong occurrence, never as a failure. One spelling makes it a compile-time fact. Structural fix over a fourth literal, per CLAUDE.md.

The old BindSingleSectionInstanceToken is therefore LEFT IN PLACE, uncalled by production code, and retired in a follow-up commit once that lane is clean — stated in the file header so a census of "single-section binders" honestly returning two is understood as deliberate rather than as an unfinished refactor.

The build-path call site, plus the deletion of the retired renderCtx.ContentData["ComponentID"] binding twenty lines above it — RFC_032 section 8's third and last. Census before deleting, with a demand control: 0 ACTIVE and 0 INACTIVE templates spell {{.ComponentID}}, against a control of 140 spelling {{.InstanceID}}. Minimal diff (~12 lines) in a historically contested file; the hunk check is re-run in the same minute as the commit, per the landmine.

edits.rationale: ORDER BY position ASC -> ORDER BY position ASC, id ASC. This query IS the canonical walk that assigns occurrences; the editor's SQL compares on (position, id). Without both halves a tie is ordered arbitrarily by Postgres and the two derivations can disagree on the same page. Blast radius measured: 2 live (page_id, position) ties fleet-wide as of 2026-08-24, BOTH cross-function, so no instance token changes value today; their current order is Postgres-arbitrary anyway.
edits.sketch:

edits.rationale: The check that proves every RenderTemplate caller binds a token. The new binder's name ends in "BindInstanceToken(" so the unanchored regex already matched it — this makes it explicit so a future \\b-anchoring cannot silently unmatch it. Verified BOTH ways: the tree-wide sweep over all tracked non-test .go files returns 0 findings, and the demand control (deleting the bind from each of the two rewired files in a scratch copy) returns exactly 1 finding each.

edits.rationale: Every case names the mutation that kills it, and the four load-bearing ones were RUN, not asserted (evidence below). The agreement test is the important one: it asserts the derived token equals InstanceTokensForPage's for the same list, including mixed case and trailing space ("FAQ " vs "faq"), which is what makes "two paths rendering the same page agree on every token" a checked property rather than a claim.

edits.rationale: THE ANSWER TO THE COUPLING OBJECTION, and the reason this design is defensible at all. It runs the REAL handleLoopExpansion over a five-section loop and feeds the REAL injected config and the REAL CollectedData to the reader, then asserts the derived token equals the canonical whole-page token for the same section. Without it, the contract could rot with both sides still compiling and the reader simply finding nothing — which is a LEGITIMATE state for this reader (it means "no loop", falling back to 0), so the failure would be silent wrong ids rather than a red test.

grounded_in: THE DEFECT IS LIVE AT THE ARTEFACT, fetched 2026-08-24 during this session (not read from a bug file): `curl -s https://gaswholesalers.com/pricing-transparency.html | grep -o 'id="c-generic-text-block[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c` returns `2 id="c-generic-text-block"`. vetcomparison.uk/how-it-works.html likewise. DB sweep the same day: 3 multi-instance pages carry a duplicated c- token in stored rendered_html. apis.uk/index.html still holds build_status='needs_rebuild', so it re-collides on its own — a repro that regenerates itself.

THE LOOP CONTRACT, VERIFIED ON A LIVE ORCHESTRATION, not inferred from the handler. Orchestration de6a6243-b575-429f-a58f-2e985c98314d (2026-08-24): all 10 injected render_component steps carry loop_item_index 0..4 and loop_name='process_sections_loop'; collected_data carries process_sections_loop_item_0..4. Across 5 sampled runs the item-key count equals the injected-render-step count exactly (5/5, 4/4, 2/2, 2/2, 6/6). Every item carries the resolved function at BOTH the top level and component.function; component.name is a DISPLAY name ("Generic Text Block" for function "generic-text-block") and is never read.

THE KEYS ARE DECLARED SURFACE, not internals — the load-bearing claim for the coupling argument. platform/orchestration/datahelpers/action_inputs.go:211-230 defines frameworkStepConfigKeys as "step-config keys the orchestrator itself reads or injects, on any step regardless of action. They are never 'unknown'", and lists loop_item_index, loop_iteration, loop_name, loop_var_name each commented "injected by loop expansion". Existing action-side readers: loop_actions.go:324 (GetIntField on loop_iteration), :352 (loop_name), :520 (the item key), call_agent.go:318, create_work_item_action.go:433/436. The dependency direction is precedented, not new.

WHERE THE FIX ACTUALLY BITES, live config 2026-08-24, measured with BOTH queries per this lane's RUNBOOK section 6. A top-level jsonb_each over workflow->steps finds ZERO render_component steps fleet-wide (control: 1,322 steps carry an 'action'), because both live steps are nested at steps.process_sections_loop.config.sub_workflow.steps.{render_section,render_from_template} in page-content-writer — exactly one active agent definition. That is also why the build path is ALWAYS a loop iteration today, which is what licenses loop-counting as the primary derivation rather than a special case.

SIZING, live DB 2026-08-24, every figure re-run on build day per the committed plan's own open question 6: 30 multi-instance (page, function) pairs; 16 of 30 repeat a slot_name (which is what kills any slot-only key and is the measurement that most argues against the plan's build-path design); 2 (page_id, position) ties, both cross-function; 2,002 non-removed page_components rows of which 11 have NULL component_id and ZERO of those sit on a multi-instance page (sizing the editor join's blind spot at zero live instances). 6 empty-id rows on 6 pages — Half B's concern, unchanged.

THE THIRD BINDING'S DELETION, censused WITH A DEMAND CONTROL, 2026-08-24: content_components rows spelling '%.ComponentID%' = 0 active AND 0 inactive; the control, rows spelling '%.InstanceID%' = 140 active. So the binding is genuinely inert and the query family can find template tokens. (The inactive arm matters: a dormant row that could be reactivated would make 'zero active' a weaker claim than it looks.)

THE TESTS WERE MUTATION-PROVEN BY RUNNING THE MUTATIONS, all against committed HEAD via scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --test. (A) loop arm reverted to constant occurrence 0 — the defect itself: loopCountsSameFunctionPredecessors AND agreesWithInstanceCounter both FAIL. (B) instanceFunctionKey loses ToLower (keeping the import used so it still compiles): agreesWithInstanceCounter FAILS. (C) loop_item_index read with a bare .(int) assertion — the float64 round-trip trap: FOUR tests FAIL. (E) the expander re-introduces a hardcoded key literal instead of calling LoopItemKey: ONLY the cross-package parity test fails. (F) the expander stops injecting loop_item_index: ONLY the parity test fails. (G) functionOfLoopItem reads component.name: parity test AND readsTheExpanderContract fail. Original restored byte-identical after each (diff verified).

A MUTATION THAT DID **NOT** KILL A TEST, reported rather than quietly dropped, because it changes what the parity test can be claimed to prove. (D) changing LoopItemKey's FORMAT leaves every test green — since the spelling is now single-sourced, writer and reader move together, so the format is no longer a thing that CAN drift: the helper is a guard in SERIES with the test. The drift that remains possible is a caller going around the helper, which is mutation (E) and which the test does catch. My first draft of that test's docstring claimed (D) as a killing mutation; running it proved the claim false and the docstring is corrected in the committed code.

PATTERN-CHECK, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Tree-wide sweep using the checker's own check_unscoped_component_render over every tracked non-test .go file (git ls-files '*.go', never a directory list): 0 findings. DEMAND CONTROL: stripping the bind call from scratch copies of the two rewired files yields exactly 1 finding each — so the 0 could have come out otherwise.

BLAST RADIUS ON rendered_html_digest, raised by the bugs_open/357 lane and MEASURED rather than argued. My change alters the bytes of a repeated component's second instance, so that md5 takes a new value on those rows. Census of consumers, non-test, whole tree: 6 writers, all computing md5($n) in the SAME statement as the bytes; 2 readers — page_component_divergence.go:68 and site_component_divergence.go:70/120 — both comparing the stored digest against the STORED bytes, plus livespec.go:203/215 with the same shape. None compares a stored digest against a fresh render, so the pair stays in lockstep and no consumer is affected. The 357 lane independently re-verified this census at their end.

VERIFIED AT COMMITTED HEAD, NOT THE WORKING TREE — and it mattered. The shared tree does not compile: another session's uncommitted load_work_item_actions.go:1605 calls an undefined ownedPageParkedItem. Every result above comes from scripts/verify-head-builds.sh with only these 9 files overlaid onto committed HEAD, where the full ./platform/orchestration/... suite passes. Baseline taken before any edit: also green.
plan.risks:
1. NO OPT-IN FLAG, AND I THINK THAT IS RIGHT — but it is the seats' call. The 2026-08-02 section 2 ruling prescribes opt-in-with-unsafe-default-OFF for new AUTHORITY on a shared seam. I judge this is not new authority: the seam already bound a token unconditionally, this changes only the VALUE from a constant to a derived count, every failure path binds the old constant, and nothing can refuse a render. A flag here would gate a better input behind a switch whose OFF position is the known defect, and would leave the mechanism unexercised — the rot this estate has been bitten by. If a seat reads the derived value itself as authority, the contained alternative is a RenderContext field defaulting to constant-0, and I would rather be told than assume.

2. THE EDITOR PATH CAN ERR HIGH, and this is the one branch that is not strictly non-worse. The canonical walk advances its counter only for sections that RESOLVED a component; a carried section (component missing, template invalid) does not advance it. The SQL cannot see template validity, so where an earlier same-function section is unresolvable the count comes out one HIGH. On the build path that is byte drift only — a distinct token, never a collision. On the EDITOR path it can hand the edited row the token the next canonical instance already holds, i.e. SWAP which partner it collides with rather than add a collision. It needs an invalid-template same-function predecessor to occur at all; it is no worse in collision COUNT than the constant 0 it replaces (which also collides with exactly one stored partner); and DetectInstanceCollisions reports either shape at assembly. Documented on the function, not only here.

3. FIRST BUILD IS FIXED; A NON-LOOP CALLER WOULD NOT BE. The loop derivation covers the first build, which the committed plan called an irreducible residue. But a future workflow that runs render_component OUTSIDE a loop, or inside a loop iterating something other than the page's ready composition, would bind occurrence 0 (today's behaviour) or a self-consistent but canonically-wrong value. Zero such callers exist today — ONE active agent definition runs the action, and the count carries its date because it goes stale BY ADDITION. A LANDMINES entry footprinted on render_component / process_sections_loop warns the author who adds the second one.

4. COMPOSITION DRIFT ON A REBUILD. The loop counts THIS build's ready sections; stored rows reflect the previous build. Where they differ around a repeated function the derived occurrence can differ from what a later canonical rerender assigns — self-consistent within the save (the same list is stored at positions i+1 in list order), and reconciled at the next full-page rerender. Never a collision.

5. TWO SINGLE-SECTION BINDERS EXIST AFTER THIS CHANGE. BindSingleSectionInstanceToken remains, uncalled by production code, because component_instance_scope.go is dirty in a concurrent lane and moving a function out from under it would repeat the passenger that drew the veto on e8c7414c. It is retired in a follow-up commit. Stated in the file header so it does not read as an unfinished refactor — but a seat may reasonably want the retirement sequenced differently.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not repair the stored damage — that is a page_rerender through the canonical walk, filed separately, and it is what makes the fix DURABLE rather than what makes it correct. It does not touch Half B (the empty-id detector and the unbound-token report), which is committed and under its own council correlation 661bcf00. And it is Go, so it is inert until the next chassis roll.
